title: Lock-Order Inversion (Classic Deadlock)
pattern: Multiple threads acquiring a common set of locks in inconsistent lexicographical or hierarchical order.
why_bad: It violates the global partial-order invariant required for deadlock-free lock acquisition, allowing a cycle of mutual blockages where each thread holds a lock needed by the other.
detection: Look for nested lock acquisitions across different threads or functions where the sequence of lock identifiers is reversed or inconsistent.
counterexample: Acquiring multiple locks under a strict global hierarchy (e.g., always locking in alphabetical or address order).
source: Herlihy 9.4, Paul McKenney 7.1.1, Clean Code Ch 13
